Why does the range extend this far?

Desktop and workstation cards differ from data-center accelerators. For reference, NVIDIA lists 96 GB for RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, while AMD lists 288 GB for MI355X. These advertised GB figures are not necessarily usable GiB; use your runtime’s reported capacity. This tool estimates memory capacity, not accelerator compatibility. Sources checked October 16, 2026.

Choose a preset to load model size, weight format, and cache architecture. Your GPU and reserve stay unchanged.

A rough capacity proxy. Training and model family matter just as much. Q4 means roughly 4-bit weights; Q8 means roughly 8-bit. These are formats, not model names. The K_M suffix identifies a quantization variant. Usually you download a different model file to change precision; this calculator only simulates it. Less precision uses less memory, with model- and task-dependent quality losses.

Optional background: Q4 formats and QAT

Q4_0 uses blocks of 32 weights sharing a scale, totaling 4.5 bits per weight including the scale. Q4_K_M uses a more elaborate block scheme and mixed tensor precisions; this calculator budgets about 4.85 bits per weight. Q4_K_M often preserves quality better for conventional post-training conversions, at a modest memory cost. Speed depends on hardware and kernels.

QAT means quantization-aware training: training accounted for reduced precision. It is a property of the model’s training, not something inferred from choosing Q4_0. A QAT Q4_0 model should not be judged by the usual post-training format ranking. Neither format alone guarantees better reasoning.

Here K means 1,024 tokens: 4K / 8K context is unrelated to Q4 / Q8 weight precision. Room for prompt, history, and output does not mean more intelligence. Lower offload moves weights and cache to system RAM in this approximation; CPU work can slow responses.

WHAT YOUR SETTINGS MEAN

Three different kinds of “better.”

01

Reasoning quality

02

Working memory

Do you need more than 8K? Short chats without large pasted documents may already fit. Conversation depth is not a token count: instructions, retained history, attachments, and output all use space. This calculator cannot see your local conversation or detect whether you are near its limit.

Check your local app’s token-usage display or runtime logs, if available, and leave room for the answer. Earlier details being missed can be a clue, but does not prove the context is full. Try 16K when you need more material in view; compare speed on the same task.

Under the hood · formulas, assumptions & sources

All memory is in GiB (2³⁰ bytes); GPU marketing GB may differ. Weights = parameter count × effective bits per weight ÷ 8. Assumed effective bits: Q3_K_M 3.9; Q4_0 4.5; Q4_K_M 4.85; Q5_K_M 5.7; Q6_K 6.6; Q8_0 8.5; FP16 16. Mixed tensors, scales, and file formats vary.

KV cache = 2 (keys + values) × layers × KV heads × head dimension × tokens × bytes per element. This cache stores previous attention calculations so generation can reuse them. It grows with active tokens; this tool budgets the full selected context because some runtimes reserve it up front. A larger configured limit alone need not slow a short prompt unless allocation or spill changes.

VRAM = GPU weight fraction + GPU cache fraction + fixed runtime overhead. GPU/cache offload is approximated as proportional; real layer placement, cache placement, batching, Flash Attention, and buffers vary. One sequence, dense text-only model, conventional full attention; no vision encoder, MoE, sliding-window savings, multi-GPU, or unified memory modeling. The RAM figure excludes CPU runtime, loading copies, OS and applications.

Comfortable: remaining VRAM ≥ desired headroom. Tight: fits the estimate but misses headroom. Spill likely: estimate exceeds VRAM; actual runtimes may offload, refuse to load, or fail. Headroom is a reserve, not additional model memory. Recommendations sample 1–72B in 0.5B steps; actual supported context must be checked against the model card.

There is no universal quality or tokens-per-second formula. Visible reasoning depends on model behavior and app support; it is not a quality score or a cache setting. Extra context can preserve relevant evidence and leave space for generated reasoning, but cannot grant learned capability.
